# T3 Code patch ledger

Every vendored file Rennet has changed from the pristine snapshot on the `t3-vendor` branch, with why. `pnpm t3:check-ledger` fails on any vendored file that differs from the snapshot and is not listed here. Paths are relative to `vendor/t3code/`. Rennet-owned files inside the tree (`UPSTREAM.json`, this file, `digests/`, any `project.json`, any `tsconfig.rennet.json`) never need a row.

Prefer extension over edit: put Rennet code outside `vendor/` and import their modules. When upstream merges a change listed here, the fold that brings it in removes the row.

| File | Reason | Upstreamable | Upstream PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts` | `thread.turn.start` (both command shapes) and the `thread.turn-start-requested` payload carry an optional `outputSchema`, so a turn can declare a structured-output contract. Rennet's board seats need one JSON board per turn. The same three shapes also carry an optional `mcpServers` (`name → { url, bearerTokenEnvVar? }`), so a caller can hand a turn its own MCP servers. The field names the environment variable holding the credential and never the credential: this command is persisted to the event store and replayed from it, and the Claude SDK puts its whole MCP option on the child's argument list. Server names are constrained to a TOML bare key because Codex writes them into a dotted config path, where a dot silently makes a nested table. The file also defines `TurnMcpServer`/`TurnMcpServers` and the two helpers every hop shares (`normalizeTurnMcpServers`, `differingTurnMcpServerNames`). | yes | pending |
| `packages/contracts/src/provider.ts` | `ProviderSessionStartInput` and `ProviderSendTurnInput` carry `outputSchema` and `mcpServers`. `ProviderService` re-decodes both and strips unknown keys, so a field has to exist on the schema to survive the hop. | yes | pending |
| `packages/contracts/src/providerRuntime.ts` | `TurnCompletedPayload` carries `structuredOutput` and `durationMs`, the two facts the SDK result frame already reports and T3 dropped. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.ts` | Copies the command's `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` onto the `thread.turn-start-requested` event it emits. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts` | Threads `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` from the turn-start event into both `ProviderSessionStartInput` (the session starts on the first turn) and `ProviderSendTurnInput`. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts` | Sets the SDK's `outputFormat: { type: "json_schema", schema }` from the session's `outputSchema`, remembers the contract on the session context, fails a later turn whose schema the live session cannot serve (the SDK fixes `outputFormat` at `query()` construction and offers no setter) and says which of the two ways it failed, and puts `structured_output`/`duration_ms` from the result frame on `turn.completed`. Merges the turn's caller-supplied `mcpServers` into the SDK's, with T3's own `t3-code` entry written LAST so it wins a name collision, remembers the set on the session context and refuses a later turn asking for a different set by the names it disagrees on — the SDK fixes `mcpServers` at `query()` construction exactly as it fixes `outputFormat`, and `strictMcpConfig` is deliberately not set. Also spawns the Claude child through the SDK's `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` hook so its stdin has an `error` listener: the SDK's own transport writes the prompt without one, and a `claude` that dies before that write raised an unhandled `write EPIPE` that killed the whole server process. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts` | `sendTurn` carries the turn's `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` into the session `resolveRoutableSession`/`recoverSessionForThread` recovers from a persisted resume cursor. Claude's SDK fixes `outputFormat` when the query is built, so a session recovered without it could never serve the turn that asked for the recovery: the adapter refused the turn as a schema mismatch, against a contract identical to the thread's own. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.test.ts` | Covers the recovery above: a stale `claudeAgent` session recovered for a turn starts on that turn's output schema, and on that turn's MCP servers. The MCP case is the only test that crosses `ProviderSendTurnInput`, which is re-decoded here and strips any key it does not declare. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts` | Forwards a turn's `outputSchema` to the Codex session runtime, and lowers caller-supplied `mcpServers` to `-c mcp_servers.<name>.url=…` plus `-c mcp_servers.<name>.bearer_token_env_var="…"`, naming the variable the daemon set and never carrying a credential. `bearer_token_env_var` is written even for a server that declared none, because Codex deep-merges every `-c` into the user's own config and offers no way to remove an inherited key — without the write, a same-named server in the user's config would point THEIR credential at this endpoint. A name the sidecar owns is dropped rather than overwritten, and the adapter states `sidecarMcpServerConfigured` rather than letting a name imply it. Codex reads its MCP configuration when the app-server is spawned, so a later turn asking for a different set is refused the way Claude's is. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts` | `buildTurnStartParams` passes `outputSchema` through to `V2TurnStartParams.outputSchema`, which the generated protocol already carries and T3 was dropping. Splits the MCP question in two: `hasConfiguredMcpServer` still answers the tool-catalog reload for any inline server, while `browserToolsAvailable` reads the new `sidecarMcpServerConfigured` option, which the adapter states. A name cannot answer it — a caller supplying a server called `t3-code` would satisfy any name test — and describing browser tools the session does not have is a lie in the Codex prompt. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts` | Projects a `turn.settled` activity from `turn.completed`, carrying the settled turn's structured output, duration, usage and cost. Nothing else in the projection carried a turn's own result, so a reader over `orchestration.subscribeThread` could not see it. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.test.ts` | Covers the new adapter behaviours above: the schema becomes the SDK's `outputFormat`, no schema means no output format, a turn asking for a different contract than its session is refused, a turn arriving on a session that holds no contract is refused as that rather than as a mismatch, and the spawn hook terminates a child whose stdin breaks instead of letting the EPIPE escape. Also covers the caller-supplied MCP servers: the header carries a `${VAR}` reference rather than a credential, T3's own server keeps the `t3-code` name against a caller that claims it, no servers means no `mcpServers` option at all, and a turn asking for a different set — including one differing only in its credential variable — is refused with the differing names. One case drives the REAL SDK through the spawn hook and reads the argument vector it built, because the `--mcp-config` serialisation is downstream of this adapter and cannot be seen by reading it. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.test.ts` | Covers the Codex leg of the caller-supplied MCP servers: the arguments name the credential variable and carry no credential, a server declaring none still gets the key written empty, a caller cannot bind or claim provenance for the sidecar's `t3-code` name, and a turn asking for a different set is refused. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.test.ts` | Covers what the reload predicate answers, and states plainly that it is name-blind by design — the browser question is settled by provenance in the integration test, not here. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexCollabRuntime.integration.test.ts` | Drives the real session runtime against the scripted app-server for the two behaviours the predicate split exists for, neither of which can be reached by calling a predicate: the tool-catalog reload happens BEFORE `turn/start`, and the turn's own developer instructions describe browser tools only when the sidecar's server is attached — including the case where a caller took the `t3-code` name. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/testFixtures/codexCollabMockPeer.mjs` | An opt-in `recordAllRequests` that appends every request the runtime sends, in order, to its own sidecar file. The existing `recordRequests` records `thread/resume` only and its file is compared exactly, so ordering assertions needed a separate record rather than a widened one. | yes | pending |
| `packages/contracts/src/orchestration.test.ts` | Covers the turn's MCP servers at the contract: an endpoint and a credential variable NAME decode, a raw credential has nowhere to live, a server name Codex could not write into its config path is refused, and so is a credential variable that is not an environment variable name. | yes | pending |
